title: Retention Flow
summary: Three post-purchase touchpoints — AI drafts follow-up, learner reviews before sending.

sections.heading: Orientation — Lesson Start
sections.subtitle: Lesson Start
sections.contentMarkdown:
- What Will You Understand? Retaining customers is not luck — following up after purchase keeps the relationship alive, and AI helps you write it quickly.
- Why Now? In the previous lesson, I explained Offer — the customer knows what they are buying. Now the question is: after the purchase, how do we keep the relationship active? A lot of weakness occurs after purchase — the customer disappears without follow-up.
- What After the Lesson? You will design a simple Retention Flow of 3 steps for one type of customer you have.

sections.heading: Tension — A Familiar Situation
sections.subtitle: A Familiar Situation
sections.contentMarkdown:
- You attract new customers, but the same people do not return. It’s not always because the product is bad — sometimes it’s because there is no follow-up after purchase.
- Follow-up does not mean being annoying. It means: ensuring they are satisfied, offering help, and reminding them at the right time.
- AI writes message drafts, personalizes the tone, and helps you ask a simple satisfaction question — you review and send.

sections.heading: Core Idea — 3 Touchpoints After Purchase — Not a Huge Campaign
sections.subtitle: 3 Touchpoints After Purchase — Not a Huge Campaign
sections.contentMarkdown:
- Touchpoint 1 — A Few Days Later: "Is everything okay? Do you need anything?" — Confirmation + a door for early complaints.
- Touchpoint 2 — After Two Weeks: Useful content or a suitable offer — not just "buy again."
- Touchpoint 3 — After a Month: A friendly reminder + an invitation to return or refer.
- A simple NPS (Net Promoter Score) question or satisfaction question ("On a scale of 1 to 5, how was your experience?") gives you a signal — and AI helps you phrase it and summarize the responses.

sections.heading: Quiz — Quick Confirmation

sections.contentMarkdown:

Design a follow-up touchpoint after purchase + draft a confirmation message
Explanation: Retention is often cheaper than acquisition. AI helps in drafting the follow-up — it does not replace the decision on timing and content.

sections.heading: Mission — 3 Retention Steps for One Type of Customer
sections.subtitle: 3 Retention Steps for One Type of Customer
sections.contentMarkdown:
Introduction: A practical design mission — not full automation. Choose one type of customer (or a persona) and write a Retention Flow of 3 steps: when, what the message is, and how AI helps you write it. No actual sending is required today — a clear plan is required. Delivery: Customer type · Step 1 (Timing + Goal) · Step 2 · Step 3 · A simple satisfaction question (one sentence). Evaluation Criteria: | Dimension | Weight | Criteria |
|-------|-------|---------|
| Realistic Flow | 60% | 3 steps with timing and goal — linked to a real customer type |
| Role of AI | 40% | Clear how it helps in drafting or summarizing |
